result:
Typecheck is clean and all 3 tests pass (the stack trace in the output is the expected 422 validation path logged by the existing `posts.search` test, not a failure).

`PostResource.toArray()` in `app/Http/Resources/PostResource.ts` was dropping `excerpt` from its returned object — every field the pages read (`title`, `body`, `authorId`, `createdAt`, `author`) was mapped through except that one, so each consumer of the resource (`/posts` index, `/posts/<id>`, the edit form, and the home page's latest-posts strip) received a payload with no `excerpt` key and rendered an empty paragraph or a blank field. The declared `PostResourceData` interface already listed `excerpt: string`, and the type error was masked because `toJSON()` casts through `super.toJSON()`, so the compiler never flagged the omission. Search kept working because it queries the `excerpt` column directly in `PostController.search` rather than going through the serialized shape. I added the missing `excerpt: post.excerpt as string` line alongside `title`, and added `tests/PostResource.test.ts`, a unit test asserting the serialized payload carries the excerpt through.
